note: Running `nestor triage` on the dogfood corpus (504 decisions at bar 0.55) produced 432 groups, 405 of which were singletons — the output was dominated by noise. The 27 multi-member groups and 8 edges (the actual signal) were buried.

decisions.question: Should the triage human output suppress singleton groups?
decisions.commitment: Yes. The human rendering shows only groups with 2+ members and appends a summary line '(N singleton group(s) suppressed)'. The JSON output keeps every cluster unchanged — callers may need the full list.
decisions.why: Singletons tell you nothing about relationships — they are the complement of what grouped. At bar 0.55 they outnumber multi-member groups 15:1, burying the edges and themed groups that are the reason a human runs triage.
